text.p: Australian-based and U.S.-listed Internet service provider OzEmail said the deregulation of Australia's telecommunications market in July next year should lead to lower access prices.
"I hope it brings more competition so there would a greater choice and that it will eventually lead to lower prices," OZEmail managing director Sean Howard told Reuters.
OzEmail currently provides Telstra, the state-owned telecommunications group, about A$30,000 per day from its customers logging onto the Internet.
OzEmail has about 82,000 customers or about one-third of Australia's 250,000 Internet surfers, Howard says, although other reports put Australia's Internet population much higher at around 500,000.
Howard expects some rationalisation among Australia's 200 plus Internet Service Providers (ISP) before deregulation on July 1 next year.

"I think there will be a shake out in the Internet Service Provider market, with providers either amalgamating or going out of business and not that I hope anyone goes out of business," he said in a telephone interview.

OzEmail had been interested in merging with service provider Access One, a unit of Solution 6 Holdings Ltd earlier this year, but the two groups could not form an agreement and OzEmail then sold its small stake in Solution 6.
Howard said OzEmail was not in acquisition talks with other providers but added it was possible that the group would look at other purchases in the forseeable future.
OzEmail shares soared to a record high of US$17 on its debut in May on the technology-laden NASDAQ exchange from its issue price of $14, but the shares have fallen heavilly since.
OzEmail shares ended unchanged at $8-3/4 on Tuesday.

Howard formed OzEmail while working for Australia's richest man Kerry Packer at the billionaire's magazine arm Australian Consolidated Press (ACP), where Howard was head and part owner of the computer publications division.
In 1992, Howard left ACP to focus on OzEmail and was later backed by two of Packer's former corporate lieutenants Trevor Kennedy and lawyer Malcolm Turnbull.
Howard owns 32 percent of OzEmail, while Kennedy and Turnbull owns 16 percent each of the Sydney-based group.
OzEmail may seek a compliance listing on the Australian Stock Exchange next year, Howard said. He added OzEmail listed in the U.S. due to its stronger Internet market following there.
"It was simply going to a market where there is a following, as in the United States there are about six Internet Service Providers that have market analysts following them," he said.
"Whereas here we would be an oddity, as there are no other companies like us listed locally," he added.
